headline: Failed House resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran without approval from Congress.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the President, under the War Powers Resolution, to end the use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities against Iran or any part of its government or military. The forces could have stayed involved only if Congress passed a declaration of war or a law authorizing military force against Iran. It would not have stopped the United States from defending itself against an imminent attack. The House voted it down on March 5, 2026.

who_it_affects.how: The President would have been directed to stop using U.S. forces in hostilities against Iran unless Congress gave specific approval.
Troops taking part in hostilities against Iran would have been withdrawn from those operations, except for self-defense against imminent attack.
Congress would have kept the deciding role in whether U.S. forces could fight Iran, through a declaration of war or a use-of-force authorization.
